newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee higher, London seen edging up.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee higher, London seen edging up.

text.p: Indonesian Robusta coffee prices were higher on Monday despite declines in London, on the back of strong demand, traders said.

They said grade four Robusta was quoted at 3,450 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, compared with 3,250 rupiah a week ago. The export price was quoted at $1,500/tonne FOB Lampung, against $1,450 last week.

"Local prices are not decreasing despite declines in London because of strong demand and expectations of lower production this year," one trader said. "Players are now convinced output will be significantly lower this year."
The traders said they expected London's benchmark July contract to open $10-$20 higher when the market opens later.

The contract rose to a new eight-week high of $1,793 a tonne last Friday on light fund and arbitrage buying, but producer selling, long liquidation and end-of-the-week squaring pulled back prices to close at $1,758, down $22.

"When London closed last Friday, New York was up one cent. So, I think London will open $10-$20 higher later on Monday," one trader said, adding that Indonesian export prices could rise as their differential with London values was ranging between $240-$260 per tonne.

"Although supply is ample at the moment, there are expectations that it would be running out by the third quarter of this year," the trader said. "The season this year is expected to be shorter than last year."

Another trader said talk of origin-selling of Vietnam's leftover beans from its harvest was putting pressure on prices, adding that there was speculation that Vietnam could have some 20,000 tonnes of coffee to sell.
"There is talk of a 'cheap sale' in Vietnam, but I don't think it will last for long," he added.
